body:
I apologize for originally missing this PR, thank you for bringing it up to our attention. You can also reach out on the [development chat](https://chat.godotengine.org/) if you feel like a PR fell through the cracks.

Thank you so much for working on this, I appreciate the work on improving the user experience and I think it's a clever way to check for the missing `TOOLS` define constant.

However, I was thinking that we may prefer to enforce that the `TOOLS` define constant is _always_ added to the user project. I haven't given this much thought yet, but I would imagine moving [`TOOLS`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.NET.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.props#L109-L110) from `Sdk.props` to `Sdk.targets` (next to [`GODOT_REAL_T_IS_DOUBLE`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.NET.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.targets#L4-L11)) would resolve the issue without the need to show error messages to the user.

The `Sdk.props` file is evaluated before the user project, and the `Sdk.targets` is evaluated after. So, by moving the define constant to `Sdk.targets`, we can ensure we append to `<DefineConstants>` **after** the user changes its value. I can't think of any downsides from this, the `TOOLS` define constant is required for the engine to work properly so I see no reason to allow users to remove it. But let me know what you think about this approach.

Looks good to me, thanks!

> Speaking about the attention, what would be a comfortable interval to notify the dotnet team in the dev chat? I don't want to introduce inconveniences by spamming the same information too frequently.

I wouldn't worry too much about a specific interval, it's really more about using the chat when you feel a PR has been overlooked for an unusually long time. Most of the time we'll be monitoring GitHub notifications, but a gentle reminder in chat is perfectly acceptable.
